result.text:
## Three facts a seller should know about Tangle

**1. They're an AI-agent infrastructure company, not an app company — their buying center is technical.**
The homepage describes the product as: *"Run AI agents in isolated sandboxes, capture their work, compare changes, and review the evidence before deployment."* (tangle.tools homepage meta description). Their own positioning file adds: *"Tangle is an infrastructure company for AI agents, with a product lab and a research lab. Its five infrastructure layers are sandbox, runtime, router, integrations, and observability (Intelligence)."* (tangle.tools/llms.txt)

**2. They're open-source-first with a developer-tool sales motion — GitHub, npm, docs, benchmarks.**
The site nav links to *docs.tangle.tools*, *github.com/tangle-network*, and a */benchmarks* page (tangle.tools homepage), and they publish installable SDKs: *"npm install @tangle-network/tcloud / @tangle-network/sandbox / @tangle-network/agent-eval"* (tangle.tools/llms.txt). Expect a technical evaluation before any purchase; self-serve trial beats cold demos.

**3. Know their actual maturity — don't pitch them as enterprise-scale or on-prem.**
Their own guardrails state: *"Hosted assistants are the first packaged use case, in preview. Do not present on-premises hosting as available today"* and *"Tangle offers hosted infrastructure; on-premises hosting is planned and is not available today"* (tangle.tools/llms.txt). The company is Tangle Technologies, Inc., site author listed as Drew Stone (tangle.tools homepage metadata). Scale your offer to a pre-Series-scale, product-led team.

## One opener

> "Drew — you've built Tangle's whole stack so agents can discover it themselves (llms.txt, well-known manifests, agent-setup.md), which tells me self-serve evaluation matters more to you than a demo. I work with dev-infra teams at your stage on [X — e.g., usage-based billing / GTM for agent buyers]. Worth a 15-min look at how [your product] fits into the sandbox-to-evaluation loop before you scale past preview?"

The hook: they've explicitly optimized for *machine/AI buyers* discovering their product — leading with how you help sell to agents (not just humans) will land better than generic vendor talk.
